title: The test harness lets git guess an identity, so an arm leaning on a guess is green wherever the host's name gives one and red only on a host without a domain
body:
Issue 0300 was this class, found on kovacs (Ubuntu, a hostname without a domain), where git refused the identity it guessed ("unable to auto-detect email address (got 'matts@kovacs.(none)')") and a releasestatus.bats arm went red that was green on every Mac: there git guesses an identity from what the host's name and resolver give (on rhadamanth, under the harness's settings, a Tailscale MagicDNS address), and the commit goes through under it.

tests/lib/test_helper.bash empties the global and system config (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, :77-78) and leaves git free to guess, so any later arm or fixture whose repository has no identity is host-shaped the same way until a host like kovacs runs it. Its comment at :76, "No identity is lost: every fixture that commits passes its own", misses devbin's own commits, which pass none (0300).

Fix (cc, after ST0011 WP02a): GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL points at a file the harness writes, holding only `[user] useConfigOnly = true`, in place of /dev/null, with harness.bats's pin of it (:105) changed to match, so a commit with no identity configured exits 128 ("no email was given and auto-detection is disabled") on every host and an arm that leans on a guess goes red where it is written. Measured in scratch by the 0300 review: with that file the commit exits 128, and a commit with an identity given exits 0. Not GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, which `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` lists and devbin's git_local_env_clear unsets; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL is on no such list. Arms that set their own GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL (releasecut.bats, releasesnapshot.bats, worktrees.bats) keep theirs. With it, the -c identity pairs that git_project's callers pass on commits and tags in its projects (macos.bats, releaseattach.bats, releasesnapshot.bats, releasestatus.bats: sixteen, as the 0300 review counted them) are redundant and go, and :76's comment says where a fixture project's identity comes from. Its run is the whole suite, since the harness change reaches every arm.

## Resolution

Fixed at 034897304eeb08c8cbcfafe4895980a5206aed4f, landed on main by devbin-vc's land-stack.sh from the tested tip 291ea882, whose paths it equals, unpushed until the 0.1.20 cut. GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL now names tests/fixtures/harness/gitconfig, a file holding user.useConfigOnly alone, in place of /dev/null, so a commit with no identity configured fails on every host, where the arm leaning on it is written; harness.bats pins the file and holds the refusal of such a commit, with a commit given an identity as its control. The -c identity pairs on commits and tags in git_project's projects went: twenty-five at the fix, where the 0300 review had counted sixteen, fourteen of them in macos.bats, two in releaseattach.bats, five in releasesnapshot.bats and four in releasestatus.bats. The three that commit in a repository git_project did not make keep theirs. test_helper.bash says where a fixture project's identity comes from, and every comment that said the suite reads no global git config now says what it reads. An arm that names a global config of its own keeps it, as releasecut.bats, releasesnapshot.bats, worktrees.bats and documentation.bats's as_reader do. It was proved on its own test, under hv's rule of 2026-11-05, in light slot 01M6N1ZZ1ANS8NGJ1CTZX9N8V2 on devbin-vc's desk: the changed arm was red as wanted in red-0302 (e8848b07), the base's code with the unit's harness.bats on top, failing its first check with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL at /dev/null; and at 291ea882 under BSD, harness.bats (35 of 35), macos.bats (47), releaseattach.bats (39), releasesnapshot.bats (20), releasestatus.bats (56), gitremote.bats (4) and documentation.bats (32) were green, each whole. Before the run, a probe in plain bash read every arm of the sixteen files whose arms commit or tag green under the harness change. The rest of the suite, which the harness change reaches, is the cut's gates', its kovacs leg's and CI's to read.
